clue.text: Reverse jacket worn by renegade

parts.note: to turn is to reverse direction
a jacket is a short coat

explanation.surface: Someone who has switched sides wears a reversible jacket, fitting for a renegade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' looks like an instruction to read something backwards, but it simply supplies a verb meaning to switch round.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat is a person who deserts one party or cause for the opposing one, which is what a renegade does.

clue.text: Carry kid on back of bike

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the next word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of bike

explanation.surface: A parent carries a child sitting on the back of a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote something is an informal synonym for carrying it about with you.

clue.text: Barred from Las Vegas boulevard, reportedly — why?

parts.note: the Strip is the famous casino-lined boulevard of Las Vegas

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said out loud, so the following word counts only for its sound

parts.note: the letter Y is pronounced like the word why

explanation.surface: Someone asks why they have been barred from the Las Vegas boulevard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barred' reads as banned, but it is the definition in the sense of marked with bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Something barred has stripes across it, so it is stripy in pattern.

clue.text: Place to take rest of meat to scoff

parts.note: ham is a cured meat
to scoff at is to mock

explanation.surface: Someone takes the rest of the meat to eat greedily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' looks like British slang for eating greedily, but here it means to jeer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hammock is a hanging bed of netting or canvas where one lies down to relax.

clue.text: Place one might call low-tech?

parts.note: surface reading: somewhere a person would describe as technologically primitive
setter's reading: a place where one might make a telephone call, an old-fashioned kiosk

explanation.walkthrough: 'Call' seems to mean describe, but it is the call made on a telephone; the kiosk is now a relic, hence low-tech.
explanation.definitionFit: A public telephone kiosk is a booth where people made calls before mobiles, now seen as old technology.

clue.text: Can't see anything at first, then shout back: "There's no way out!"

parts.note: someone who can't see is blind

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the preceding word only

parts.note: opening letter of anything

indicators.note: back means the word before it is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to yell is to shout

explanation.surface: A frightened person, unable to see, yells that they are trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind alley is a dead-end street, one from which there is no exit except the way you came.

clue.text: Informal defender of the net?

parts.note: surface reading: a casual guardian of the internet
setter's reading: the player who guards the goal net, named in a colloquial short form

explanation.walkthrough: 'The net' suggests the internet, but it is the net behind the goalmouth in football or hockey.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the colloquial short form for a goalkeeper, the player who protects the goal.

clue.text: Brew up to face trouble

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so the words before it are stirred into a new order

parts.note: letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone makes a brew before facing up to trouble, the classic British response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brew up' looks like one phrase, but 'Brew' alone is the definition and 'up' starts the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A brew is British informal for a hot drink, especially a pot or mug of tea.

clue.text: Empty and gloomy after short break

indicators.note: after says the first word given here follows the one given at the end of the clue

parts.note: hol is a British short form of holiday
feeling low is feeling gloomy

explanation.surface: Someone feels empty and depressed after only a brief holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty and gloomy' reads as two moods, but only 'Empty' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hollow has nothing inside it, so it is empty within.

clue.text: Sample Beyoncé track from the past

indicators.note: a sample is a small part taken from something larger, so the letters lie within the next word

parts.note: the letters run inside the singer's name at the start of this phrase

explanation.surface: A producer samples an old Beyoncé song for a new record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sample' sounds like music production, but it signals letters hiding inside the singer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Once as an adjective means former, describing something belonging to an earlier time.

clue.text: Obviously, with leader gone, I'm standing in very soon

indicators.note: standing in means taking someone's place, so a new piece fills the vacancy
the leader is the opening letter, and gone means it is dropped

parts.note: eminently means conspicuously or obviously
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone announces they will obviously be standing in as leader very shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: The E at the front of the word for obviously is replaced by I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Imminently means about to happen at any moment, so very soon.

clue.text: Sporty American boy's the ultimate young horseman

parts.note: in American slang a jock is an athletic young man

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so only the closing letter of each word is kept

parts.note: last letter of the
last letter of young

explanation.surface: An athletic American lad is the best young rider of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ultimate young horseman' reads as praise, but 'ultimate' takes the end letters of 'the' and 'young'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jockey is a professional rider in horse races, a kind of horseman.

clue.text: They take people to fish round and about

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one word goes outside the other

parts.note: kippers are smoked herrings

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word before it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Anglers take people out fishing round and about the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' sounds like taking people somewhere, but it means seize. The fish wraps round the reversed little word.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnappers seize and carry people off by force, usually for ransom.

clue.text: Greens back BBC covering article on energy put into gas production

indicators.note: back means the following letters are read from the end to the start
covering means wrapping round something, so one piece holds another inside

parts.note: taken as written
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: a production is something made, so the letters before it are built into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A news item about the Green party getting coverage on the BBC and energy production from gas.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed broadcaster wraps round A to make CABB; E is put into a rearranged GAS to make AGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabbages are leafy vegetables, and greens is a common collective name for such vegetables.

clue.text: Peered at man briefly, then passed on

indicators.note: briefly asks for a shortened form, so the name is cut down

parts.note: Stuart is a man's name
passed on is a euphemism for died

explanation.surface: Someone stared at a man for a moment, and then he died.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuart is shortened to the nickname Stu.
explanation.definitionFit: To have studied something is to have looked at it closely and carefully, as one does when peering.

clue.text: Measures cooking span for chicken product

definitions.text: Measures cooking span for chicken product

parts.words: Measures cooking span for chicken product
parts.note: surface reading: steps taken to time the cooking of some chicken dish
setter's reading: the hen's product is what is being boiled, and the device times it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken product' suggests nuggets or a cut of meat, but it is what a hen lays.
explanation.definitionFit: This kitchen device, often a small sand glass, tells you when a boiled breakfast item is done.

clue.text: Sending away old flame, I return love note

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
taken as written

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word after it is written backwards

parts.note: love means zero in tennis scoring
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone banishing a former lover sends back a love letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love note' reads as a billet-doux, but the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Exiling someone means banishing them, sending them away from their home country.

clue.text: Mean girl only just avoiding disaster

definitions.note: a phrase describing the noun's situation; the answer names such an event

parts.note: near is an old word for stingy, or mean
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A spiteful girl narrowly escapes catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' reads as unkind, but it is the sense of tight-fisted.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is an incident where an accident or collision is narrowly avoided.

clue.text: Renamed foreign snake

indicators.note: foreign means strange or unfamiliar, so the letters are made to look different

parts.note: letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An exotic snake has been given a new name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snake' looks like a noun for a reptile, but it is a verb meaning to wind.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to follow a winding course, as a river or path snakes across country.

clue.text: Angry speech foreign secretary managed to interrupt

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into something, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: William Hague was the UK Foreign Secretary from 2010 to 2014
to run something is to manage it

explanation.surface: A minister's furious address is cut short by a manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A harangue is a long, aggressive and ranting speech of criticism.

clue.text: Mighty river warrior

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the vast South American river
second meaning: one of a legendary race of female fighters

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests one powerful river fighter, but the words split into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the largest river by volume and to the women warriors of Greek myth.

clue.text: Dad has deposit account to begin with in years when he gets his wages

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: in places those letters inside the following piece

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letters of the words before it

parts.note: opening letters of deposit and account

explanation.surface: Dad pays into a deposit account at the start of each year, when his salary arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Payday is the day on which an employee receives their salary.

clue.text: Quietly left to pursue organised care package

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so this piece comes after the next

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so these letters are set in a new order

parts.note: letters taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A care package is quietly sent off after being organised.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel is something wrapped up for sending by post, the same as a package.

clue.text: Activist's party regain force

parts.note: a camp is a faction or party with shared views

indicators.note: to force something is to wrench it out of shape, so the word before is rearranged

parts.note: letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A political activist's party seeks to take back power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'force' looks like a noun meaning power, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaigner works actively for a cause, which is what an activist does.

clue.text: Skip start

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to leap or pass over something
second meaning: a sudden flinch of surprise

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to skip the start, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to leap over or omit something and to give a sudden startled movement.

clue.text: Knave's flag?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the playing card ranking below the queen
second meaning: a small flag flown at a ship's bow

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive suggests a rogue's banner, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The knave in a pack of cards is also called this, and it is the name for a ship's national flag.

clue.text: Study programme for Ascot say?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a series of lessons or lectures
second meaning: Ascot is an English racecourse, so an example of a horse-racing track

explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a famous racecourse in Berkshire, England; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a programme of education and the track over which a race is run.

clue.text: Duty to accommodate Queen in train

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: excise is a tax or duty on goods
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A sovereign is housed while on a rail journey as part of official duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' suggests a railway, but it is a verb meaning to drill or work out.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise is to train the body, or to drill soldiers, through repeated practice.
